key_insight: A high-dimensional neural network potential can reproduce DFT-level energetics and structural behavior of martensitic NiTi, enabling realistic finite-temperature simulations at large atomistic scales.
engineering_relevance: This model supports predictive design and analysis of NiTi shape-memory and deformation mechanisms by making nanosecond-scale, hundred-thousand-atom simulations computationally feasible.
method: Trained an HDNNP on DFT reference data for martensitic NiTi.
Validated against equilibrium structures, elastic constants, stacking-fault energies, and vibrational spectra.
Used molecular dynamics to study structural evolution across temperatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate reproduction of subtle B19' versus B33 energy differences on the order of meV/atom and a strongly anisotropic stacking-fault energy landscape.
watch_item: Performance is tied to the DFT training domain, so transferability to unseen compositions, defect states, or phase conditions should be checked carefully.
paper_title: A high-dimensional neural network potential for finite-temperature phenomena in NiTi martensite
